en: you had this great advice to when you were at Stanford, I think it was,
zh: 你以前在斯坦福的时候给过一个很棒的建议，我记得是这样说的，

en: which is, I wish to you pain and suffering.
zh: 那句话是：我祝你经历痛苦和磨难。

en: Do you remember that? Yeah.
zh: 你还记得吗？记得。

en: Fantastic. What's your advice to young people around what they should be studying?
zh: 好。那对于年轻人该学什么，你有什么建议？

en: So if they're sort of about to leave high school, because now those are the kids that are at this like really native,
zh: 比如说，如果他们正准备高中毕业，因为现在这批孩子正处在这样一个非常原生的时代，

en: they haven't made a decision about college, what to study, if at all go to college.
zh: 他们还没有决定是否要上大学、学什么，甚至要不要上大学。

en: How do you guide those kids?
zh: 你会怎么引导这些孩子？

en: What would you tell them?
zh: 你会对他们说什么？

en: I still believe that deep science, deep math, language skills, as you know,
zh: 我依然相信，深入的科学、深入的数学，还有语言能力，正如你知道的，

en: language is the programming language of AI now.
zh: 语言现在就是人工智能的编程语言。

en: The ultimate programming language. And so as it turns out, it could be
zh: 是终极编程语言。所以结果可能会是，

en: that the English major could be the most successful.
zh: 英语专业的人反而可能成为最成功的那一批。

en: And so I think I would just advise, whatever education you get,
zh: 所以我想我会建议，无论你接受什么样的教育，

en: just make sure that you're deeply, deeply expert in using AIs.
zh: 都一定要确保自己非常非常擅长使用人工智能。

en: One of the things that I wanted to say with respect to jobs,
zh: 还有一件关于工作的事我想说，

en: and I want everybody to hear it, that in fact, at the beginning of the deep learning revolution,
zh: 而且我希望大家都能听到，那就是在深度学习革命刚开始的时候，

en: one of the finest computer scientists in the world, deeply, deeply, I deeply,
zh: 世界上有一位最顶尖的计算机科学家之一，一位我极其、极其、极其尊敬的人，曾经预测过，

en: deeply respect, predicted that computer vision will completely eliminate radiologists.
zh: 计算机视觉会彻底取代放射科医生。

en: And that the one field he advises everybody to not going to is radiology.
zh: 而且他说，放射学是他建议所有人都不要去读的领域。

en: 10 years later, his prediction was 100 percent right.
zh: 10年之后，他的预测在技术层面上百分之百正确。

en: Computer vision has been integrated into all of the radiology technologies and radiology platforms in the world,
zh: 计算机视觉已经被整合进了全球所有放射学技术和放射平台，

en: 100%. The surprising outcome is the number of radiologists actually went up
zh: 百分之百都整合进去了。可令人意外的是，放射科医生的数量实际上反而增加了，

en: and the demand for radiologists is skyrocketed.
zh: 而且对放射科医生的需求还在飞速上升。

en: The reason for that is because everybody's job has a purpose and it's task.
zh: 原因在于，每个人的工作都同时包含目的和任务。

en: The task that you do is studying the scans, but your purpose is to helping the doctors,
zh: 你的任务是研究这些扫描影像，但你的目的是帮助医生，

en: helping the patient diagnose disease.
zh: 帮助病人诊断疾病。

en: And so what's surprising is, because the scans are now being done so quickly,
zh: 所以令人惊讶的是，因为现在扫描可以做得非常快，

en: they could do more scans, improving healthcare, but doing more scans more quickly allows patients to be onboarded a lot more quick,
zh: 他们就能做更多扫描，从而改善医疗服务；而更快地做更多扫描，也能让患者更快被接收，

en: treated a lot more quickly.
zh: 更快得到治疗。

en: And as it turns out, because hospitals enjoy making money too, they're doing more scans,
zh: 而且结果是，因为医院也希望赚钱，所以他们会做更多扫描，

en: they're treating more customers and more patients, the revenue's going up and guess what?
zh: 他们会服务更多客户和病人，收入也会上升，然后你猜怎么着？

en: In a country that grows faster, productivity increases, a wealthier country can put more teachers in the classroom,
zh: 在一个增长更快、生产力持续提升的国家里，一个更富裕的国家可以在教室里配备更多老师，

en: not less teachers in the classroom.
zh: 而不是更少的老师。

en: You just give every one of those teachers a personalized curriculum for every student in the room.
zh: 你只需要给教室里的每一位老师，为班上每一个学生都配上一套个性化课程。

en: It makes them all bionic and leads to a lot more.
zh: 这会让他们都像装上了外挂一样，带来更多可能。

en: Every single student will be assisted by AI, but every single student will need great teachers.
zh: 每一个学生都会得到AI的辅助，但每一个学生依然都需要优秀的老师。
